persona.who: 25, Tamil-Singaporean analyst at a bank, first in family to go to university, got promoted early, feels she doesn't belong in the room.
persona.note: got promoted ahead of people with MBAs. in every meeting I think they're going to find out I'm just the girl from the HDB whose dad drove a taxi. I over prepare for everything and still feel sick before presenting

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call not feeling good enough, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from the verdict you keep passing on yourself to the part of you that can stand in the room without rehearsing.

week_beats.steady: You hold that a success is something that happened, not who you are.

understanding.core_struggle: Promoted ahead of peers, she feels like a fraud from an HDB background and over-prepares to hide it.
understanding.mirror: You out-prepared them to get here, and now you're over-preparing to stay here.
understanding.insight: The promotion was real. The fear that it was a mistake is what keeps you over-preparing and still feeling like the girl from the HDB.

queries.hook: The feeling of being exposed as a fraud despite your success, and the dread of being found out in every room. I feel like an imposter.
queries.diagnose: When a result goes wrong, the mind turns against itself; self-blame grows from believing the outcome alone measures our worth.
queries.steady: A failure is something that happened, not who you are; no one who tries to do good is ever lost.
queries.act: Lift yourself up instead of pushing yourself down; learn what this taught you, make amends where you can, and begin again.
queries.story: A woman who rose without the right credentials, faced her own doubt, and found the courage to stand in her truth.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् । सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
verse.line: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.
verse.translation: One should not give up the work suited to one's nature, Kaunteya, even if it has faults; for all undertakings are clouded by faults, as fire is by smoke.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'never change jobs'. It answers perfectionism, not a reason to stay where you're harmed.

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that no work is flawless. He says you could not abandon the work that suits your nature just because it has faults. Every undertaking is clouded by flaws, just as fire is always surrounded by smoke. The point is to do the work that fits you, with all its imperfections, as an offering.
verse.for_you: You are rehearsing your life before you live it. Krishna is telling you to let the smoke of your over-preparing be there, and still show up for the work that is yours, without demanding it be perfect first.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.for_you: A mistake is something you did, not who you are; no one who tries to do good is ever lost.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: पातितोऽपि कराघातैरुत्पतत्येव कन्दुकः । प्रायेण साधुवृत्तनामस्थायिन्यो विपत्तयः ॥
verse.line: A ball knocked down bounces back up. For good people, setbacks rarely last.
verse.translation: A ball struck down by the hand flies right back up. As a rule, the misfortunes of those who live rightly do not last.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.
verse.misuse: Not a promise that suffering is always short, or that people who suffer long did something wrong.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.for_you: The self is untouched by your mistakes; it was never stained and cannot be made less, whatever you have done.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying on the ground after losing his kingdom, defeated and ready to surrender. She tells him not to hold himself in contempt or settle for a small life. She asks him to set his mind on what is truly good and to pull himself together. She is saying that a loss is an event, not a verdict on who he is. It is a call to stand up and act, not to shrink from what he has become.
verse.for_you: You are in the room where the promotion sits, real and done, and you are rehearsing a speech to prove you belong there. Try setting your mind on the work itself instead of the verdict you keep passing on your HDB roots. Let the facts of the day hold you for a moment.

verse.speaker: Dharmavyadha (the righteous meat-seller)
verse.setting: In Mithila, a meat-seller famed for wisdom teaches a proud ascetic what goodness really is.
verse.sanskrit: पापं चेत्पुरुषः कृत्वा कल्याणमभिपद्यते / मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो महाभ्रेणेव चन्द्रमाः
verse.line: Turn to doing good after a wrong, and you come out like the moon from behind a cloud.
verse.translation: If a person who has done wrong turns to doing good, he is freed from all his wrongs, like the moon coming out from behind a great cloud.
verse.why: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.

prasang.title: Vyadha Gita: the butcher who taught a sage
prasang.summary: A proud ascetic, Kaushika, is sent to learn from a meat-seller in Mithila. The butcher teaches him plain goodness: don't return evil, repent and resolve, keep envy away, care for your parents, and don't spend your one life making enemies.
prasang.lesson: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.

verse.meaning: In Mithila, a meat-seller named Dharmavyadha teaches a proud ascetic named Kaushika about true virtue. The ascetic has come looking for great wisdom, but the butcher offers something simpler. He says that if a person turns to doing good after a wrong, they are freed from it, just as the moon comes out from behind a cloud. The butcher's point is that wisdom is not in grand gestures but in ordinary work done honestly, like caring for your parents.
verse.for_you: You have turned your hard work into a promotion, and now you are doing good in your job. Let your over-preparation be your honest work, not a mask to hide behind. Trust that your background does not cancel the good you are doing now.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
verse.line: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, even done imperfectly, than the duty of another well done. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.
verse.why: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.
verse.misuse: Not 'stay in the role your family or birth assigned you'. It's about being true to your own nature and calling.

prasang.title: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna is caught between two ways of living: following his own nature, which feels risky and imperfect, or taking on a role that looks better from the outside but does not fit him. Krishna tells him that walking his own path, even if he stumbles, is safer and truer than trying to live someone else's life perfectly. The borrowed role is full of fear because it asks you to perform a part that is not yours.
verse.for_you: You are rehearsing a part that was never written for you. The promotion was real, but you are still trying to play someone else's script. Let your own work, however imperfect, be enough. You do not need to over-prepare to prove you belong in the room.

story.title: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is
story.story_hook: Everyone had named a number, and the one who could actually do it was sitting quietly at the back.
story.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
story.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

anchor.speaker: Jambavan
anchor.setting: On the southern shore no one can leap the ocean; old Jambavan turns to the silent Hanuman.
anchor.sanskrit: बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिपुङ्गव। विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न सज्जसे।७।।
anchor.line: You have the strength, the brains and the courage. Why are you holding yourself back?
anchor.translation: Your strength, intelligence, energy and courage stand out among all beings, best of monkeys. Why do you not step up?
anchor.why: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

prasang.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
prasang.story_hook: Everyone had named a number, and the one who could actually do it was sitting quietly at the back.
prasang.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

story.hook_title: Everyone said how far they could leap, and Hanuman sat silent at the back
story.teaser: Everyone said how far they could leap, and Hanuman sat silent at the back
story.for_you: You are like Hanuman, sitting at the back while others shout numbers. You have the strength and the mind for this leap. The fear of being exposed is not a sign to hold back. It is a sign that you are ready to show them what you can do.

script: You are carrying a promotion that is real, and a fear that it is a mistake. You are rehearsing your life before you live it, and the anxiety is exhausting you.
Arjuna sits on the battlefield, unsure if he is the right person to lead. Krishna looks at him and speaks. And Krishna replied:
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत्, सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः.
In plain words: Don't abandon work that suits you just because it has flaws. Every undertaking has some, like fire has smoke.

Krishna tells Arjuna that no work is flawless. He says you could not abandon the work that suits your nature just because it has faults. Every undertaking is clouded by flaws, just as fire is always surrounded by smoke. The point is to do the work that fits you, with all its imperfections, as an offering.
Before your next presentation, let your preparation be enough. Do not demand a perfect performance to prove you belong. Show up for the work as it is.
Let the smoke be there, and still walk through the door.

depth.life: You are rehearsing your life before you live it. You stand before your work, ready to present, and you are already sick with the performance. You are trying to erase the HDB background with perfect slides and a flawless script. The promotion is real, but your mind is still proving it was a mistake.
depth.points: Every undertaking is clouded by faults, like fire by smoke. The flaw is not the problem. The problem is the demand that your work be flawless before you can accept it. You are trying to smoke out the fire completely, but the smoke is the price of the heat.
depth.practice: Before your next presentation, stop rehearsing for five minutes. Sit with the feeling of being an imposter. Let the smoke be there, and then walk into the room.
depth.question: What would it look like to let the smoke stay?
